script.base: PHI@NYG on 2025-10-09 is a PHI -7 control game, not a shootout: total 40.5, PHI implied 23.8, NYG implied 16.8, outdoors at night. Base flow is PHI leading by halftime on Barkley (43 carries, 119 yards, 2.77 YPC in weeks 3-5) and Hurts runs (18 carries, 107 yards) with Smith (21 targets, 203 yards, 178 air) ahead of the inefficient Brown (27 targets, 159 yards, 322 air). NYG stays Skattebo-first early (50 carries, 198 rush yards and 17 targets, 117 rec yards, -17 air in weeks 3-5) because a 16.8 team total does not support a four-man pass stack. Pace should be moderate; garbage time is only a moderate risk at a 7-point spread, not a 14-point blowout flag.
script.flip1: PHI scores early, the lead hits double digits, Hurts and Barkley run the clock, and Brown/Smith/Goedert yards stall the way a favorite's pass game dies in a 38-21 type script. NYG then abandons Skattebo's 16.7 carries a game, Dart throws into PHI's 31% blitz (NYG EPA/db -0.21 vs blitz), and Slayton's absence (out, hamstring; 14 targets, 105 yards, 194 air in weeks 3-5) forces Nabers, Robinson, and Johnson to carry a trailing pass game.
script.flip2: Dickerson (PHI G, out, ankle) wrecks the PHI run efficiency that the 5.70 NYG YPC allowed would otherwise gift Barkley, NYG hangs around behind Skattebo and Dart's 18/112 rush sample, and both teams throw. Smith and a Slayton-boosted Nabers become live, and 40.5 is threatened. A third flip, weather dragging this outdoor night game under, cannot be priced because the forecast was not saved.

matchup.pressure: NYG blitz rate 35%. PHI EPA/db is 0.01 versus blitz and 0.05 versus no blitz, so Hurts is not a blitz-panic QB in this sample and Brown's 322 air yards are not automatically dead against the blitz. PHI blitz rate 31%. NYG EPA/db is -0.21 versus blitz and -0.10 versus no blitz, so pressure that gets home should kill Nabers/Slayton-type deep shots (Nabers already at 3.3 yards per target on 170 air yards) and boost Skattebo and Johnson checkdowns.

PHI also bleeds the right side of the field at 6.69 YPA. NYG's pass defense has no clean side; all three locations sit at 6.5-plus YPA.
matchup.overlap: The textbook overlap is PHI's run game into NYG's 5.70 YPC, but it is not a clean Barkley rush-yard bet: Barkley is at 2.77 YPC on 43 carries in weeks 3-5 (119 yards, about 39.7 a game, under the 46.5 stand-in), Hurts has taken 18 carries for 107 yards in the same games, and Dickerson is out. The overlap that still holds for a listed market is Barkley receiving into two missing NYG linebackers, with Dickerson forcing the quick game (12 Barkley targets, 98 yards, 24 air in weeks 3-5). NYG's overlap is Skattebo, already 17 targets at -17 air, into PHI's blitz and a non-elite 4.73 YPC run defense, with right-side 6.69 YPA as the pass-side soft spot if Dart looks that way for Robinson or Nabers.

pre_mortem: It is the morning after PHI@NYG and both leans lost. Barkley finished under 24.5 receiving because PHI led with Hurts runs (he already has 18 carries and 107 yards in three games) and the checkdowns never came: the 6- and 9-yard games were the role, 31 and 58 were the outliers, and two backup linebackers did not matter in a shell that was never charted. Skattebo finished under 90.5 because Carter played, PHI's 4.73 YPC defense and 17 explosive runs allowed were good enough, Dart was as bad versus the 31% blitz as the -0.21 EPA/db says, and the dump-offs went to Johnson (14 targets) or Bellinger (6 targets, 71 yards) instead of the back. The 16.8 implied total was the tell that NYG did not have the plays, and the 59-yard scrimmage game, not the 121, was the template. No real price was shown, so beating a season median was never a book edge. That counter is real, which is why both legs are leans and the data check is a flag, but it is not stronger than the usage-plus-injury read, so the legs stay for the human instead of being cut.
slip_story: One PHI@NYG story: favorite controls a 40.5 outdoor night game, Dickerson's absence forces Barkley checkdowns over 24.5, and the NYG +7 trail keeps Skattebo's rush-plus-receiving work over 90.5 alive after carries fade. That is a favorite-control, both-backs-underneath stack. It is not a shootout (no Smith/Brown/Nabers overs together), and it does not mix a total under with same-game pass overs. Two legs, no touchdowns, one market per player, no depth-WR legs, no Dillon or Tracy filler. Re-run if Eluemunor, Dean, Carter, or a late Barkley/Skattebo inactive hits.
